_comment: Atlas company facts — realistic trial. Anonymized placeholder data. Not investment advice.
name: ASML Holding
business: ASML designs and manufactures photolithography equipment used in semiconductor fabrication. Its EUV systems are required for producing the most advanced chips. The installed base generates recurring service and upgrade revenue.
competitive_position: Sole supplier of EUV lithography systems globally. Competitive moat is reinforced by decades of accumulated IP, engineering knowledge, and deep customer integration. No credible EUV alternative exists within a 5-7 year horizon.
revenue_model: Capital equipment sales plus long-term service and upgrade contracts. Service revenue provides recurring income and is less cyclical than equipment orders.
key_risks: US export control restrictions limiting sales to China — impact on long-term bookings is an open research question
Customer concentration among a small number of leading-edge chip manufacturers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel)
Long development cycles create execution risk if EUV yield improvement milestones are missed
Cyclical semiconductor capital expenditure patterns create order book lumpiness
evidence_gaps: Quantified impact of US export restrictions on 2025-2027 revenue and bookings
Customer concentration risk: dependence on TSMC as primary EUV customer
High NA EUV adoption timeline and revenue contribution
notes: Evidence gap: export control revenue impact not yet resolved. No action warranted without completing this evidence review. Thesis remains intact pending resolution.
